content: For individuals with newly diagnosed diabetes, the following C-peptide levels can help guide the classification of diabetes type: If the C-peptide level is greater than 600 pmol/L, the diagnosis is most likely type 2 diabetes. If the C-peptide level falls between 200 and 600 pmol/L, the results are considered indeterminate. In such cases, it may be appropriate to repeat the C-peptide test after a period of 5 years to reassess. If the C-peptide level is less than 200 pmol/L, the diagnosis is most likely type 1 diabetes.
